Bug_Details: LocalDate.plus() and minus() does not work with Durations. LocalDate represents civil time (years/months/days), so java.time.Period is the appropriate thing to add or subtract instead.
Bug_Explanation: The code attempts to use LocalDate.plus() with a Duration object. However, LocalDate is meant to work with periods (years/months/days), and Duration represents a time-based amount in terms of seconds and nanoseconds, making it inappropriate for LocalDate.
Trigger_Explanation: The testShowBugWithDuration and testShowBugWithNegativeDuration methods both trigger the bug by calling showBug with a long value representing days, which is converted to a Duration. This causes an exception because LocalDate.plus() is used with a Duration, which is inappropriate for LocalDate.
